nectar filtering results in species-poor, clustered yeast communities that differ from the potential species pool in terms of species richness and phylogenetic structure.
nectar filters pollinator-borne yeasts, so that the community eventually established there is a predictable subset of the species pool, and that the realized community is phylogenetically clustered.

H. foetida nectar filtering of bee-borne inocula is a strong determinant of community assembly in the nectar of this species, and that this process is driven by a combination of environmental filtering (the harshness of nectar as a niche), and phylogenetic constraints (the phylogenetic related of yeasts in nectar).
